title: U.S. House · Massachusetts's 9th District
area: Southeastern Massachusetts and Cape Cod, including New Bedford, Fall River, Plymouth, Barnstable and the islands of Martha's Vineyard and Nantucket.

context.text: Incumbent Bill Keating defeated Craig Swallow in the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary. R. Tyler MacAllister won the Republican primary unopposed.

candidates.name: Bill Keating
candidates.ballotNote: Won the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary against Craig Swallow.

summary.text: Bill Keating is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Massachusetts's 9th District. A lawyer, he served in both chambers of the Massachusetts legislature and as Norfolk County district attorney before winning election to Congress in 2010. He serves on the House Armed Services and Foreign Affairs committees.

background.text: Born September 6, 1952, in Norwood, Massachusetts, and raised in Sharon.

Earned a bachelor's degree (1974) and master's degree (1982) from Boston College and a law degree from Suffolk University (1985). Wikipedia describes the master's as an MBA and says he later became a partner at the law firm Keating & Fishman.

Elected to the Massachusetts House of Representatives in 1976, at age 24, and served there until 1984, when he won a Norfolk and Suffolk seat in the Massachusetts State Senate; he served in the State Senate into the late 1990s.

Elected Norfolk County District Attorney in 1998, defeating the incumbent, and was reelected without opposition in 2002 and 2006. His office launched a Norfolk Anti-Crime Council and a drug court pilot program, and laid the groundwork for a Children's Advocacy Center in the county.

Won the open 10th District seat in the 2010 election, defeating Republican state Rep. Jeff Perry, and took office in January 2011. After redistricting in 2012, he ran in the redrawn 9th District, which he has represented since 2013.

Serves on the House Armed Services Committee and the House Foreign Affairs Committee, where he is the top Democrat on the Subcommittee on Europe. His work has focused on district issues such as the fishing industry and nuclear safety, according to Wikipedia.
A co-sponsor of Medicare for All in 2019, he is seeking an eighth term in 2026; he won the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary over Craig Swallow.
Lives in Bourne with his wife, Tevis; they have two adult children, according to Wikipedia.

priorities.text: Supporting responsible gun-control legislation, including background checks before all gun purchases and opposing the legal availability of high-capacity, military-grade firearms.
Treating access to high-quality, affordable health care as a basic human right and building on the Affordable Care Act.
Investing in conservation and coastal restoration, including wastewater management on Cape Cod.

positions.summary: Supports background checks before all gun purchases and opposes the legal availability of high-capacity, military-grade firearms; has cosponsored bills including the Fix Gun Checks Act and the Large Capacity Ammunition Feeding Device Act.
positions.quote: He supports background checks before all gun purchases, in addition to stemming illegal possession or transfer of firearms and improving safety technologies like personalized weapons and trigger locks. Bill strongly opposes the legal availability of high-capacity, military-grade firearms, which are strictly weapons of war.

positions.summary: Describes himself as pro-choice, cites a consistent 100% rating from NARAL Pro-Choice America, and supports preserving Title X family-planning funding.
positions.quote: Bill Keating is pro-choice and proud to have consistently received a 100% rating from NARAL Pro-Choice America.

positions.summary: Says access to high-quality, affordable healthcare is a basic human right and supports building on the Affordable Care Act.
positions.quote: Bill believes that access to high-quality, affordable healthcare is a basic human right.

positions.summary: States support for raising the federal minimum wage.
positions.quote: He strongly supports raising the minimum wage to $10.10.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs and the House Committee on Armed Services, including the Cyber, Information Technologies and Innovation Subcommittee and the Intelligence and Special Operations Subcommittee, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

Served as Ranking Member of the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Europe in the 118th Congress (2023-2024) and chaired the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Europe, Energy, the Environment and Cyber in the 117th Congress (2021-2022).

candidates.name: R. Tyler MacAllister
candidates.ballotNote: Won the September 1, 2026 Republican primary unopposed.

summary.text: R. Tyler MacAllister is the Republican nominee for Massachusetts's 9th District. A Mattapoisett charter-fishing business owner, he has held local elected and appointed roles in town government, including multiple terms on the Select Board. He had not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and no campaign website was found.

background.text: Born in Massachusetts; a 2021 report says he is originally from Cape Cod and has lived in Mattapoisett with his family for about 20 years.

Holds a bachelor's degree in marine biology from UMass Dartmouth and an MBA from UMass, according to a 2021 local news report. He owns a charter fishing business and has worked as a consultant to the renewable energy industry.

Served eight years on the Mattapoisett Select Board, left to apply for town administrator, and lost a close race to return to the board. He later held a five-year seat on the Conservation Commission and served on the Plymouth County Advisory Board and the town Finance Committee.
Won a July 2021 special election to the Select Board, 471 votes to 224, to fill the unexpired term of a member who had died, and was reelected in May 2023 to a three-year term.
Ballotpedia lists him as serving on the Mattapoisett Select Board as of 2026, while August 2026 news reports describe him as a former board member.
